correctness.rationale: Open-edge path connectivity and union inclusion–exclusion establish the exact objective; strict concavity balances outside margins; an exact adjacent-distance polynomial increment yields each unique nonunit root; a strict adjacent ratio comparison orders every root and proves no skips. Exact-rational enumeration independently checked 483 edge-subset cases plus 26,946 parameter-placement comparisons. This is an analytical proof for every integer n>=4 and 0<p<1; it does not treat correlated contacts or time-to-discovery.

originality.rationale: Actual published-finding corpus queries, archived same-slot claims, archival full-text epidemic surveillance literature and cross-field facility reliability methods were compared by implication. The closest 2017 exact-importance paper uses time to discovery on n<=7, and the 2018 frequency-detection study reports empirical correlations, not all-path adjacent-step transition thresholds. Residual generic-reliability and full-text access risks are recorded. Originality is self-review and not independently certified.
residual_risks: A formally equivalent two-site network reliability/coverage optimization could have appeared under geometric covering terminology unlocated by current searches.
The 2023 temporal-cascade general algorithm was not inspected in full; no NOT_COVERING assertion is inferred from its abstract alone.
A general facility-location theorem could imply this special case despite not stating the explicit staircase in accessible descriptions.
Independent literature verification is not performed.

value.rationale: The objective is the epidemiologically motivated chance of catching at least one stochastic outbreak with two constrained sentinel sites. A complete sharp allocation phase diagram replaces heuristic centrality spacing: each separation from floor(n/3)+1 through n-1 has its own nonempty unique-optimum interval, and transmission probability creates n-dependent exact transition roots. It informs the sensitivity of optimal sentinel deployment to transmission assumptions, not merely a toy finite numerical improvement.
